skill.name: skills-creator
skill.description: Creates and maintains Agent Skills with concise triggers, templates, and progressive disclosure. Use when creating or updating SKILL.md files.
skill.summary: Guides creation and maintenance of Agent Skills for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
skill.author: Emz1998

security_audit.summary: Static analysis mostly flagged command examples, documentation links, and skill storage paths in reference material. I found no prompt injection, malicious network behavior, or automatic command execution. The main remaining risk is expected functionality: generated skills can persist under .claude/skills and affect future agent behavior.

remediation.issue: Persistent skill creation can alter future agent behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation for target scope and path before writing under .claude/skills. Refuse overwrites unless the user approves them.

remediation.issue: Bundled references include destructive removal commands.
remediation.suggestion: Replace rm -rf examples with safer delete guidance that verifies the exact skill directory before removal.

remediation.issue: Reference files include shell command examples that scanners flag.
remediation.suggestion: Label commands as examples and prefer descriptions when execution is not required by this skill.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Agent Skill Creation
semantic_findings.description: The workflow tells the agent to save generated skills under `.claude/skills/[skill-name]/SKILL.md`. This can change future agent behavior in the project, so path scope and overwrites need explicit user approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: SKILL.md directly instructs saving a new SKILL.md under the project skill directory and lists that saved file as acceptance evidence. This is expected functionality, but it is a real persistence risk if used without confirmation.

content.value_statement: Creating reusable AI skills requires clear triggers, safe scope, and concise reference structure. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through maintainable SKILL.md files.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of SKILL.md files with required name and description fields.
Applies progressive disclosure rules for reference files and supporting resources.
Provides a reusable template for skill frontmatter, workflow, rules, and acceptance criteria.
Checks naming, description, file path, and trigger quality against skill guidelines.
Explains Claude Code personal and project skill storage patterns.
limitations: It does not include executable scripts or automated validation tools.
It requires the user to define the skill purpose, audience, and trigger conditions.
Reference content may need updates when Claude Code skill behavior changes.
It can create local skill files only when the agent has filesystem access.

use_cases.title: Create a Personal Skill
use_cases.description: Build a focused Claude Code skill for a repeated personal workflow, with clear triggers and concise instructions.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Skills
use_cases.description: Create project skills that follow consistent naming, reference structure, and acceptance criteria across a repository.

use_cases.title: Improve Existing Skills
use_cases.description: Review and update an existing skill for progressive disclosure, clearer scope, and safer file organization.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a new Agent Skill for my repeated workflow. Ask for any missing purpose, trigger, and output details before drafting it.

prompt_templates.title: Draft From Requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these requirements to create a SKILL.md file. Include a concise trigger description, workflow, rules, and acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Refine an Existing Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this existing skill for trigger clarity, progressive disclosure, reference depth, naming, and duplication. Apply focused improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-File Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a skill with supporting references for this complex workflow. Keep SKILL.md concise and place detailed guidance in direct reference files.

output_examples.input: Create a skill for reviewing database migrations.
output_examples.output: The result defines a migration review trigger, a focused review workflow, safety rules, and acceptance criteria for generated skill files.

output_examples.input: Improve this skill so Claude loads less context.
output_examples.output: The result moves detailed guidance into direct reference files and keeps the main skill focused on routing and essential rules.

output_examples.input: Build a team skill for release note drafting.
output_examples.output: The result creates a project-ready skill with a clear description, consistent terminology, and guidance for release note quality checks.

best_practices: Define both what the skill does and when it should trigger.
Keep SKILL.md concise and place detailed guidance in direct reference files.
Confirm the target skill path before creating or replacing files.
anti_patterns: Do not create vague descriptions that match too many unrelated requests.
Do not hide important instructions in deeply nested reference files.
Do not overwrite existing skills without explicit user approval.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It helps create and maintain Agent Skills with clear triggers, concise workflows, and supporting reference structure.

faq.question: Does it run scripts?
faq.answer: No. The skill contains markdown instructions, references, and a template. It does not include executable script files.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation covers Claude Code skill folders, SKILL.md structure, and common maintenance workflows.

faq.question: Can Codex use the guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. Codex can use the same authoring principles when creating or reviewing skill files in a repository.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the skill purpose, target user, trigger phrases, expected workflow, and any required reference material.

faq.question: What is the main safety concern?
faq.answer: Generated skills can affect future agent behavior, so confirm the path and review content before installation.
